_: STORY THREE -- The Rock That Answered Back (Vanarinda Jataka).
THE PRIMITIVE IS `rock`, and it is the first one about the WORLD rather than about two
characters touching. carry put a stick in two beaks; ride put a monkey on a crocodile;
both are promises about a single frame. This one is a promise about the FILM: the stone
the monkey has crossed by twice a day for years is the same stone, in the same place, on
the same waterline, every time we see it -- and on one night it stands a hand's width
higher, because there is a crocodile lying on it. If that does not hold, the monkey's
suspicion is nonsense and the story has no engine.
So a shot cannot say much about the rock. Its sprite, its x, its height and the waterline
are film-level, in `rig` below, and a shot may write only:
"rock": {}                    the rock as it always is
"rock": { "on": "croc-lie" }  tonight
There is no field for moving it, resizing it or floating it. What film.js then checks is
that the renderer honoured that, that anything lying on the rock is ON it, and -- across
the whole film -- that both versions actually appear and differ by enough for a child to
see. "Higher than it has ever sat" means nothing to someone never shown how it usually
sits, so the film failing to show both is a failure the assertions catch.
NOT DRAWN YET. The rig, the shot list and the assertions are done and were verified on
stand-in art; the stone, croc-lie and the five plates need one `npm run assets` run with
GEMKEY set. Nothing else is outstanding.
KNOWN GAP: `water` is a promise ABOUT the plate that nothing checks. The rig asserts the
rock sits on the declared waterline; it cannot see where the water actually is in the
picture. A still caught this once already -- 0.605 put the stone on the far horizon
instead of in the river -- so look at one shot after the real plates land, and expect to
adjust this number once.
THE CAST IS BORROWED. monkey and crocodile were drawn for story two and cost this film
nothing; the only new drawing is the stone. That is the 69-characters-for-323-stories
arithmetic in docs/02 §7 actually happening.
